To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
Ophiostoma ips is a faster growing fungus than Amylostereum areolatum, and it is able to outcompete A. areolum in pine wood and in artificial media.
the fungus O. ips introduced by I. grandcicollis into pine trees prevents the growth of A. areolum, the fungus deposited by S. noctlilio into pine trees.

the bark beetle I. grandicolis, disrupts S. noctlilo biological control programmes in pine plantations by introducing the fungus, O. ips, that out competes A. areolum in the wood, and thus prevents the nematode, B. siricidicola from surviving and reproducing.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the interaction between three species: a bark beetle (I. grandicolls), the woodwasp S. nocticilio and the nematode (B. siricidicola), which are all involved in the biological control of S. nocilio, a pest of pine plantations.
the interactions of three species, two of which are invasive and one of which is a biocontrol agent.

the interactions between the introduced biological control agent, B. siricidicola; the introduced pest, I. grandcollis, and its fungal symbiont, O. ips; and the native woodwasp, its fungus, A.  areolatum.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the fungus Ophiostoma is a threat to the biological control of Sirex.
the bark beetle, I. grandi-collis, disrupt the biological control of the pine woodwasp, by the nematode B. siricidicola via fungal symbionts.
the fungus, Ophi. ips, is a major factor contributing to the decline of the biological control programme for the woodwasp S. nocticola.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
O. ips is a superior competitor to A. areolum in pine trees, but that the latter fungus is a superior competitor in the soil, and that the two fungi have similar competitive abilities in pine bark.
the fungus A. areolum is a key component in the S. nocticilio lifecycle, and the fungus O. ips is a key factor in disrupting the S. noticilio lifecycle.
the bark beetle, I. grandicollis is disrupting the biological control of S. noctilio by the nematode, B. siricidicole.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the bark beetle, I. grandicolis, is a threat to S. noctlilio biocontrol because of the competitive interactions between the fungi O. ips, which is introduced by the beetle, and A. aerolatum, which is deposited by S. nocticlio.

the bark beetle, I. grandicollis can disrupt the biological control of S. noctilio by competing with A. areolatum for space within the trap trees, and by preventing the nematodes from feeding on the fungus.

the fungus O. ips, associated with I. grandcillisis, is an antagonist of A. areolum, a symbiont of S. nocillio, and thus a potential antagonist to the nematode, B. siricidicula, used in the biological control of S. notillio.
